newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-TAX AFFAIR HANGS OVER YEBOAH COMEBACK, SAYS MANAGER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TAX AFFAIR HANGS OVER YEBOAH COMEBACK, SAYS MANAGER.

text.p: The threat of major tax problems in Germany hangs over Leeds United striker Tony Yeboah as he prepares to return from a long injury layoff in the next month, the player's manager said on Thursday.

The Ghanaian forward, who has not played since last season because of knee surgery, is involved in an investigation over alleged tax irregularities at his cash-strapped former club Eintracht Frankfurt. Yeboah has refused to comment.
"Of course it is an influence. He hasn't said anything but I know what he is like," his manager Joachin Leukel said.
"If you have the threat of paying a million marks in tax -- just to pick a figure out of the air and we don't know any figures yet -- of course it is going to influence you."

Second-division side Eintracht, already seven million marks ($4.63 million) in the red, were thrown into crisis on Tuesday when their chairman and treasurer quit after alleged tax problems with former captain Yeboah.

Eintracht managing director Detlef Romeiko said Frankfurt public prosecutors were investigating irregularities relating to alleged payments made to Yeboah, believed to be around two million marks ($1.32 million).

Yeboah, who has been successful in England since he left Eintracht under a cloud two seasons ago, has recently started full training with the English premier league side and hopes to back playing within the next three weeks, Leukel said.
